addenda.discovered_during: the implementing sitting's §12.1 re-probe (the gate did its job)
addenda.finding: the News Stream carries SHORT FLASH ITEMS beside the briefings: a price-change flash (id 604014, 'Gold is down by 2%', body 'Gold decreased 2% to 3562.37 USD/t.oz', 37 chars) rotated onto the top of the stream ~16:20 UTC, pushing the briefing 603757 to the second slot and 603349 out of the 3-slot window
addenda.consequence_for_the_parser: the capture scope is the BRIEFING-QUALIFIED items (body >= 200 chars, observed 910-948); flash items (body < 200) are skipped, never stored, never an alarm — the owner's §11 Q1 answer ('just the box of briefing + title') defines the scope. The h2#description cross-check binds to the TOP BRIEFING-QUALIFIED item, not the raw top slot.
addenda.detail_page_finding: the article's own body lives in the detail page's <meta name="description"> — full, verbatim, rotation-proof. Verified byte-identical to the commodity page's stream copy for 603757 (939 chars, True) and matching the census record for the rotated-out 603349 (948 chars). The detail page's own News Stream is just the GLOBAL current stream (flash included) — it does NOT reliably contain the article's own body once the item rotates out.
gate_reactions: a page whose stream has zero briefing-qualified items AND no (or short) h2#description -> structure alarm (the login/interstitial negative's semantics, preserved)
a page whose stream has zero briefing-qualified items but a real h2#description (>=200 chars) -> the quiet fire (the stream window rotated past the briefing; the page's own summary is unchanged)
h2 present + briefing items present + h2 != top briefing body -> structure alarm (template drift)
